newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Trygg-Hansa unveils higher 1996 profit, buy-back.
newsitem.headline: Trygg-Hansa unveils higher 1996 profit, buy-back.

text.p: Swedish insurance company Trygg-Hansa AB on Thursday posted a 31 percent rise in 1996 profits and unveiled plans to buy back two billion crowns ($270 million) worth of shares which was welcomed by the market.
Trygg-Hansa said its two largest shareholders, Trygg-Hansa Liv and SPP, had guaranteed the share buy-back at a price three percent under the market price.

"Trygg-Hansa's two largest owners, Trygg-Hansa Liv and SPP, have pledged to offer so many shares that the buy-back can be fully carried out regardless of whether other shareholders agree to take part," Trygg-Hansa said in a statement.
An announcement of the buy-back drove the insurer's shares up 13 crowns to 169 before they settled down to close flat at 156 crowns.
Analysts said the buy-back plan did not come as a complete surprise and did not exclude the possibility of the insurer making an acquisition in Sweden's insurance market later.
"They still have excess capital so they can still make strategic moves," Nils Ringdal, insurance analyst at Dresdner Kleinwort Benson told Reuters.
Last May Swedish Trygg-Hansa made an unsuccessful 1.5 billion crown bid for rival WASA Sak which was rejected when WASA Liv and WASA Sak decided to merge instead.
One Swedish-based analyst said WASA, Sweden's Lansforsakringar or Finnish insurer Sampo were possible future partners for Trygg-Hansa.

"Looking ahead one or two years, who knows? Previously there has been speculation about the Finnish Sampo and Trygg-Hansa has been cooperating with them. But for now I think they're focusing on core operations," the analyst said.
Trygg-Hansa said some internal changes in 1996 charged its result with an 875 million crown restructuring item.

For the year the company posted a pre-tax profit of 2.43 billion crowns from 1.85 billion in 1995 which was below market expectations of 2.61 billion crowns. The result did not include acquisitions Trygg-Banken, Fri Placering and Trygg Fonder.
The company and most analysts were pleased with the result.
Trygg-Hansa said there was stable result trend for Swedish non-life insurance despite lower premium volumes and results for the non-life unit rose 30 percent to 750 million crowns.

"Through the agreement with Trygg-Hansa Liv and our successful asset managment, we can now sharpen our focus on the important, growing savings and life insurance market by bringing together all our activities in this area in a separate company with a broad product programme," Trygg-Hansa president and chief executive officer Lars Thunell said in a statement.
A London-based analyst at a U.S. investment bank said the bank had a very strong buy recommendation on the share.

"The turnaround story is that even in a weak market -- there's a lot of pressure on premiums in the Swedish market -- Trygg-Hansa managed through extensive cost-cutting to maintain a very good result," the analyst said.
Ringdal said: "The internal restructuring will give significant improvements in efficiency and that will offset more than what I expect in premium reductions in the future."
Trygg-Hansa proposed a dividend payment for 1996 of 2.50 crowns compared to 2.00 crowns in 1995.
